ANSCER reports conditional FCC approval for three mobile robots

The company says its AR250, AR650 and AR1250 models received conditional approval as it works toward US market access.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗18 September 2026English editorial summary
Story

Three models named in the announcement

ANSCER Robotics says the AR250, AR650 and AR1250 received conditional FCC approval effective 18 September 2026. The report is a company announcement distributed through RoboticsTomorrow.

What it means for US operations

According to the announcement, the approval allows the company to pursue the equipment authorisations needed for US import and sales, subject to domestic manufacturing and supply-chain transparency conditions.

The approval remains conditional

The announcement distinguishes conditional approval from unconditional equipment authorisation and ties it to manufacturing commitments and continuing reporting. It should not be interpreted as an exemption from all requirements.

Applications for the robots

The AR family moves materials in warehouses, factories and intralogistics operations. The parent company is based in Bengaluru, India, while its Plano, Texas operation handles North American sales and service.
